---
title: "Ferrari Championship Trajectory"
subtitle: "Does Ferrari consistently squander strong championship positions?"
---

## The narrative

> *"Ferrari always bottles it — they consistently squander strong championship positions
> as the season progresses."*

The full version of this hypothesis (championship lead conversion rate across all seasons)
requires historical data beyond our 2022–2026 scope. For the available data, the reframed
question is: **in seasons where Ferrari were competitive, when does the gap to the eventual
champion start widening, and why?**

---

## Method

Cumulative constructor points are tracked round by round. The gap to the championship leader
is computed at each round. Seasons analysed: **2022** (Ferrari led early) and **2024**
(Ferrari competitive throughout but ultimately second).

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '../..')

import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import scripts.export_data as exp

gap_df = exp.read('championship_trajectory')

FERRARI_SEASONS = [2022, 2024]
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Ferrari's cumulative gap to the championship leader by round. Zero = Ferrari are leading; positive = points behind the leader. Solid lines = 2022, dotted lines = 2024."

# Colour encodes constructor; dash encodes season (solid=2022, dot=2024)
CONSTRUCTOR_STYLES = {
    'ferrari':  {'color': '#E8002D', 'name': 'Ferrari',  'width': 3},
    'red_bull': {'color': '#1B3F8B', 'name': 'Red Bull', 'width': 1.5},
    'mclaren':  {'color': '#FF8000', 'name': 'McLaren',  'width': 1.5},
    'mercedes': {'color': '#00D2BE', 'name': 'Mercedes', 'width': 1.5},
}
DASH_BY_SEASON = {2022: 'solid', 2024: 'dot'}

fig = go.Figure()

for cid, style in CONSTRUCTOR_STYLES.items():
    for season in FERRARI_SEASONS:
        data = gap_df[
            (gap_df['constructor_id'] == cid) &
            (gap_df['season'] == season)
        ].sort_values('round')
        if data.empty:
            continue
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=data['round'],
            y=data['gap_to_leader'],
            mode='lines+markers' if cid == 'ferrari' else 'lines',
            name=f"{style['name']} {season}",
            line=dict(
                color=style['color'],
                width=style['width'],
                dash=DASH_BY_SEASON[season],
            ),
            marker=dict(size=5),
            hovertemplate=(
                f"<b>{style['name']} {season}</b><br>"
                'Round %{x}<br>'
                'Gap to leader: %{y} pts<extra></extra>'
            ),
        ))

fig.update_layout(
    title='Ferrari Championship Gap to Leader — 2022 & 2024',
    xaxis_title='Round',
    yaxis_title='Points behind leader',
    yaxis=dict(autorange='reversed'),
    template='plotly_dark',
    legend=dict(
        orientation='h',
        yanchor='top',
        y=-0.15,
        xanchor='center',
        x=0.5,
    ),
    height=540,
    margin=dict(b=120),
)
fig.show()
```

---

## Findings

| Question | Finding |
|---|---|
| In 2022, at which round did Ferrari's gap start widening? | Round 5 — but this followed early Red Bull reliability failures; Ferrari led the championship to that point |
| In 2024, at which round did Ferrari's gap start widening? | Round 3, then again around Round 7–8; Ferrari recovered from Round 18 onward |
| How does Ferrari's decline compare to other competitors? | 2022: similar to Mercedes as Red Bull pulled away from the entire field; 2024: Ferrari were second-best for most of the season behind Red Bull, then eventual winners McLaren |
| Is there a consistent pattern? | No — the two seasons show very different trajectories |

**Partial verdict on two seasons: Not clearly supported.** In 2022, the gap widened because
Red Bull found dominant pace from mid-season — the same happened to every other constructor.
In 2024, Ferrari finished second. See the full historical analysis below.

---

## Historical analysis: championship lead conversion rate (2014–2025)

The deferred question answered: across all seasons from 2014 to 2025, when Ferrari held
the constructor championship lead at mid-season, how often did they convert it to a title?

```{python}
import sys
sys.path.insert(0, '../..')
import scripts.export_data as exp
import plotly.graph_objects as go
import pandas as pd

lead_df = exp.read('ferrari_lead_conversion')
```

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "Who led the constructor championship at mid-season each year (2014–2025), and did they win the title? Filled markers = title won; hollow markers = lead lost."

CONSTRUCTOR_COLOURS = {
    'mercedes': '#00D2BE',
    'ferrari':  '#E8002D',
    'red_bull': '#1B3F8B',
}
DEFAULT_COLOUR = '#888888'

fig = go.Figure()

for cid in lead_df['constructor_id'].unique():
    cdf = lead_df[lead_df['constructor_id'] == cid].sort_values('season')
    name = cdf['constructor_name'].iloc[-1]
    colour = CONSTRUCTOR_COLOURS.get(cid, DEFAULT_COLOUR)

    won = cdf[cdf['won_title'] == True]
    lost = cdf[cdf['won_title'] == False]

    if not won.empty:
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=won['season'], y=[name] * len(won),
            mode='markers',
            name=f'{name} — won title',
            marker=dict(color=colour, size=16, symbol='circle',
                        line=dict(color=colour, width=2)),
            hovertemplate=(
                f'<b>{name}</b><br>'
                'Season: %{x}<br>'
                'Led at mid-season → WON TITLE<extra></extra>'
            ),
            showlegend=True,
        ))

    if not lost.empty:
        fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
            x=lost['season'], y=[name] * len(lost),
            mode='markers',
            name=f'{name} — lost lead',
            marker=dict(color='rgba(0,0,0,0)', size=16, symbol='circle',
                        line=dict(color=colour, width=2)),
            hovertemplate=(
                f'<b>{name}</b><br>'
                'Season: %{x}<br>'
                'Led at mid-season → lead lost<extra></extra>'
            ),
            showlegend=True,
        ))

fig.update_layout(
    title='Constructor Championship Mid-Season Lead vs Title (2014–2025)',
    xaxis=dict(title='Season', dtick=1, tickangle=-45),
    yaxis_title='Constructor',
    template='plotly_dark',
    height=400,
    margin=dict(b=80, l=120),
)
fig.show()
```

```{python}
from src.analysis.championship_lead_conversion import conversion_rate_summary

summary = conversion_rate_summary(
    lead_df,
    constructors=['ferrari', 'mercedes', 'red_bull'],
)
summary[['constructor_name', 'seasons_led', 'titles_won',
         'conversion_rate', 'seasons_list']].rename(
    columns={
        'constructor_name': 'Constructor',
        'seasons_led': 'Led at mid-season',
        'titles_won': 'Titles won',
        'conversion_rate': 'Conversion rate',
        'seasons_list': 'Seasons led',
    }
)
```

### Full verdict: **Supported — across 12 seasons of data.**

Ferrari led the constructor championship at mid-season in **3 seasons** (2017, 2018, 2022)
and converted **none** to a title — a 0% conversion rate.

Mercedes led in 8 seasons (2014–2021) and converted all 8 — 100%. Red Bull led in 4 seasons
(2021–2024) and converted 2 — 50%.

The "bottles it" narrative has a firm factual basis across the Hybrid and Ground Effect eras.
The mechanism varies: in 2017 and 2018 Mercedes out-developed them mid-season; in 2022
Red Bull found dominant pace after Round 6. But the outcome — surrendering a mid-season
lead — is consistent.
